messages:
Alex Chen: hey team :wave: I'm wrapping up my first-day checklist but hit a blocker. On WSL2 (Ubuntu 22.04) asdf python 3.11 fails to build complaining about openssl headers. I tried apt install build-essential python3-dev but still seeing errors. What's the recommended dev setup for Linux folks here? Do we prefer linuxbrew/homebrew on WSL or apt packages? Also my dotfiles didn't symlink so I don't have .env.local with local REDWOOD_* vars — who should I ask to get those or the template?

Tia Ramos: welcome Alex! :tada: For WSL we usually recommend using linuxbrew for parity with macs, but the python build issues are almost always missing libssl-dev and the right openssl path. Can you paste the exact error? Also the dotfiles repo is private at https://git.internal/redwood/dotfiles — if you don't have access ping @Jason.

Alex Chen: here's the tail of the error when running `asdf install python 3.11.4`: 
```
ERROR: Can't find OpenSSL headers. Make sure to install libssl-dev (or openssl-devel) and set CPPFLAGS/LDFLAGS if using nonstandard prefix.
clang: error: linker command failed with exit code 1 (use -v to see invocation)
```
I have libssl-dev installed but maybe it's the brew openssl path?

Jason Patel: @Alex Chen if you installed linuxbrew it puts libs under /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/opt/openssl@3. Try exporting before build: 
```
export LDFLAGS=\"-L/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/opt/openssl@3/lib\"
export CPPFLAGS=\"-I/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/opt/openssl@3/include\"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH=\"/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/opt/openssl@3/lib/pkgconfig\"
```
Then `asdf uninstall python 3.11.4 && asdf install python 3.11.4`. That fixed it for me on WSL.

Sam Gupta: +1 to Jason. Also make sure you have zlib1g-dev, libbz2-dev, libreadline-dev, libsqlite3-dev installed — python build wants those. For dotfiles: @Jason can add you to the dotfiles repo and there's a `bootstrap-wsl.sh` script that symlinks things and writes a `.env.local.template` you can copy.

infra-bot: note: Alex Chen added to group `dev-oncall` (auto) — check access request if you still can't reach dotfiles.

Alex Chen: thanks all — I installed the dev packages and set the env flags, reinstalled python and it succeeded. I also ran the bootstrap script after Jason added me to the repo (thanks!). Quick followup: what are the minimum REDWOOD_ env vars I should have locally so I don't accidentally hit prod endpoints? I saw references to REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_ENV.

Tia Ramos: good question. Locally we use REDWOOD_ENV=development and REDWOOD_API_KEY is a dummy key for local-only features. You should set: 
- REDWOOD_ENV=development
- REDWOOD_API_KEY=local_XXXXXXXX (we have a generator in the dotfiles repo)
- REDWOOD_REGION=us-west-2 (optional for testing routing)
- LOCAL_REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379 (if running redis)
If you're unsure, set only REDWOOD_ENV and run things — prod secrets are never in dotfiles. We'll add a short WSL troubleshooting note to the new-hires README.

Alex Chen: perfect, I'll paste the short steps into the README and submit a small PR: 1) install apt build deps, 2) install linuxbrew, 3) export openssl flags, 4) asdf install, 5) run bootstrap script. Thanks everyone! :raised_hands:

Tia Ramos: awesome — ping me the PR when it's up and we'll merge. Happy first week!
